summary.text: The Yellowstone hotspot is a volcanic hotspot in the United States that has driven large-scale volcanism in Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Oregon and Wyoming.
As the North American Plate moved over it, a series of caldera-forming eruptions shaped the eastern Snake River Plain.
It now lies under the Yellowstone Caldera, created by the Lava Creek supereruption 640,000 years ago.

facts.label: Kilgore Tuff eruption
facts.value: 1,800 km³ of ash, 4.5 million years ago

items.prompt: About 10 to 12 million years ago, a Yellowstone hotspot eruption buried around two hundred rhinoceroses in ash. Where were they?

options.label: Right at the rim of the erupting caldera
About 1,000 miles downwind, in Nebraska
Along the Pacific coast, west of the volcano
In a lake inside the caldera itself

items.explain: The Bruneau-Jarbidge eruption dropped a foot of ash at Ashfall Fossil Beds in northeastern Nebraska, 1,000 miles downwind.

items.prompt: The eastern Snake River Plain runs roughly parallel to the direction the North American Plate moves. Why?

options.label: A river carved it as the plate tilted
Glaciers ground it out in that direction
Two plates are pulling apart along it
It tracks the plate's path over the hotspot

items.explain: The hotspot formed the plain through a series of caldera eruptions as the plate moved over it, so the track follows the plate's motion.

items.prompt: In the Snake River Plain, younger basalt lava lies on top of older rhyolite lava and ignimbrite. What sequence does that record?

options.label: Rhyolite first, then basalt after passing the hotspot
Basalt first, then rhyolite pushed up from beneath
Both erupted together in one single huge event
Rhyolite slowly weathered into basalt over time

items.explain: Rhyolite and ignimbrite erupted as the lithosphere passed over the hotspot; later volcanoes covered the plain with young basalt flows.

items.prompt: As the hotspot passed beneath what is now Nevada and Oregon, how did it affect the local variety of life?

options.label: It wiped out nearly all local species
It merged habitats into one large range
It raised variety by splitting up habitats
It had no lasting effect on wildlife

items.explain: It increased local beta diversity by fragmenting connected habitats and making the terrain more varied.

items.prompt: Since its last supereruption, what has Yellowstone been doing?

options.label: Nothing at all; it has been fully dormant
Lava flows, smaller blasts and steam explosions
Two more supereruptions of similar size
Shifting west, away from the hotspot

items.explain: Non-explosive lava eruptions and less violent explosions have occurred since, along with steam explosions such as one that left a crater at Mary Bay.

items.prompt: Ash from the Bruneau-Jarbidge eruption landed far to the east across the Great Plains. What carried it there?

options.label: Rivers flowing east from the volcano
Prevailing westerly winds
Pyroclastic flows racing downhill
Ocean currents along the coast

items.explain: Prevailing westerlies laid distal ashfall over a vast area of the Great Plains.
